bounded_cause_not_withdrawn.record_bounded_cause: MEASURED CAUSE, CEILINGED TO THIS LAYER AS BUILT: the layer never asked about the gap. On de-kapitalverletzung it mined ZERO corpus vocabulary for both under-covered concepts (kapitalverletzung, uberwachungspflicht: mined == [] and stems == [] for each, with 0 holder documents for their prefixes in the miner's joined German view of 640 documents), so all 12 emitted terms expand concepts the baseline already covers (aktive, arbeitgebers, eingriff, fursorgepflicht); no emitted term derives from either gap concept. The per-language sample is cross-language polluted BY CONSTRUCTION: CorpusSample.build joins citation_string_de/fr/it into every benchmark row regardless of row language, so 960 of 960 benchmark rows carry a non-empty Italian citation string, 960 carry a French one and 960 a German one, and 1 of 180 emitted terms occur in NO own-authored document of their query's target language while occurring in another language's own text (e.g. petty-theft-dismissal::it:november); a further 11 of 180 terms are strictly more frequent in another language inside the miner's JOINED sample, which is exactly the join effect. The independent auditor's own witness (quoted, attributed, auditor-computed) records the same mechanism with named terms: "CorpusSample.build() joins text_head + citation_string_de + citation_string_fr + citation_string_it into every benchmark row regardless of the row's language. Witness: 21 of 421 French documents in the sample carry Itali...". Those bare-term queries DID return rows (10 of 15 added searches returned >=13 rows, 6 returned a full 50-row page), so the shape retrieves; it retrieves terms sourced from the wrong concepts and a language-polluted sample, and the composition is slow: 10 of 15 added calls breached the frozen <30.0s per-search budget (max 83.505s, sum 600.569s). Across the frozen legs the candidate-only channel recovered 0 of 9 missing frozen authority ids.
